bootstrap.description:
provisioning of the participant context, its signing key and its credentials.
Without this, a deployed identityhub is inert: it holds no participant, no key in vault and no
credential, and every DCP flow fails. The steps are the ones documented in
doc/DSP_INTEGRATION.md, run in-cluster and idempotently instead of by hand from a workstation.

rotation.description:
replacement of the signing key, keeping the same alias and DID fragment. There is no
overlap window: the moment the key is replaced everything signed with the previous one stops
verifying, so this is opt-in, runs as its own Job and never as an upgrade hook. Enable it,
let it run, set it back to false.

enabled.description:
should the rotation Job be rendered. The rotation is not atomic: the old keypair is

exits without publishing anything. Nothing wrong is ever served - the DID document is only
updated after the key is safely stored - but the participant is left unable to sign until
the Job is re-run, which is safe to do and picks up where it left off.

credentialSync.description:
sidecar that keeps the identityhub's copy of a credential in step with the Secret the
vc-operator maintains. The identityhub holds its own copy of everything a DCP connector
presents, and a copy pushed once at deploy time expires on its own schedule and takes the DCP
lane down with nothing having changed in the cluster.

It runs inside the identityhub pod and writes over localhost on purpose: the Identity API is a
component-internal API, so the only thing allowed to write to it is the pod that owns it. The
sidecar does not speak OID4VCI - obtaining and renewing the credential stays with the
vc-operator, which writes it to a Secret; this only mirrors that Secret into the identityhub.

enabled.description:
should the sidecar be rendered. It only mirrors the credential into a participant context
that already exists, so on its own it does nothing: `identityhub.bootstrap.enabled` has to be
set as well, or the sidecar will keep reporting a 404 for the participant. The two switches
are separate because a context is also provisioned by hand or by an earlier release, and such
a deployment wants the sidecar without the Job.
enabled.title: enabled

id.description: id the credential is stored under in the identityhub
id.title: id

key.description: key within that Secret holding the raw JWT
key.title: key

resyncSeconds.description:
how often the mounted Secret is re-read. The kubelet refreshes mounted Secrets on its own,
so this is the only thing standing between a renewal and the identityhub seeing it; there is
no watch on the Kubernetes API and therefore no RBAC to grant.
resyncSeconds.title: resyncSeconds

secretName.description:
Secret holding the credential, as written by the vc-operator. Defaults to
identityhub.bootstrap.credential.secretName.
secretName.title: secretName

credentialSync.title: credentialSync

credentialWatchdog.description:
the identityhub's own credential watchdog, which re-requests expiring credentials from a

checkPeriodSeconds.description:
`edc.iam.credential.status.check.period`, in seconds. 0 or less disables the watchdog.
Off by default because the credentials in this chart come from an OID4VCI issuer (Keycloak)
via the vc-operator: there is no DCP issuer service for the identityhub to ask, so leaving it
on only produces a failing request every period.
checkPeriodSeconds.title: checkPeriodSeconds

renewalGracePeriodSeconds.description:
`edc.iam.credential.renewal.graceperiod`, in seconds: how long before expiry renewal is
triggered. Upstream defaults to a week, which for a credential that only lives a week means
it is considered renewable from the moment it is issued - keep this a fraction of the
credential's lifetime.
renewalGracePeriodSeconds.title: renewalGracePeriodSeconds

customCaCerts.description:
extra CA certificates the identityhub has to trust, as a map of file name to PEM content.
They are imported into a copy of the JVM truststore by an init container, so they extend the
bundled roots instead of replacing them. Needed to reach a vault, an issuer or a counterparty
that uses a private CA.
extra CA certificates the identityhub has to TRUST, given as PEM inline: the CA of a vault,
of an issuer or of a counterparty that does not use a publicly trusted certificate. These are
not the certificates that identify this participant - those come from cert-manager and are used
straight from their Secret. Keys become filenames and, through them, truststore aliases. Use
this for a CA that does not exist in the cluster as an object; otherwise prefer
`customCaCertsFrom` and skip the copy.
customCaCerts.title: customCaCerts

customCaCertsFrom.description:
the same, but read from Secrets and ConfigMaps that already exist in the cluster, so a
cert-manager Secret can be pointed at directly instead of having its PEM copied into values.
Both sources can be used together. Each entry names either a `secret` or a `configMap`:

  customCaCertsFrom:
    - secret: mp-operations.org-tls   # keys default to [ca.crt]
    - secret: some-issuer-tls
      keys: [ca.crt, tls.crt]
    - configMap: corporate-root-ca    # no keys: every key in the ConfigMap

`keys` defaults to `ca.crt` for Secrets on purpose. A kubernetes.io/tls Secret also carries
tls.key, which does not belong in this pod and which `keytool -importcert` fails on, taking the
init container down with it. Named keys are projected as `<source>-<key>` so that two sources
cannot collide on a filename, which in a projected volume is a mount failure rather than a
warning.
customCaCertsFrom.title: customCaCertsFrom

tracing is active the deployment gains an init container that copies

volume, mounts the volume read-only into the IdentityHub container,

environment variables rendered by the `dsc.otel.env` helper.

# Provides credential revocation infrastructure for Verifiable Credentials issued by Keycloak.
# See https://github.com/adorsys/status-list-server for upstream documentation.

tracing.description:
global distributed-tracing configuration used by every component that
supports OpenTelemetry. The values under this block are fed into the
`dsc.otel.env` template helper and rendered as the standard `OTEL_*`
environment variables on each workload. Flipping `tracing.enabled` off
disables tracing everywhere; per-component toggles live under each
subchart's `tracing:` key and default to the global value.

autoInstrumentation.description:
auto-instrumentation via the OpenTelemetry Operator. When enabled,
renders an `Instrumentation` CR that the Operator's mutating webhook
uses to inject language-specific agents into annotated pods. Requires
`opentelemetry-operator.enabled: true` and cert-manager.

enabled.description:
master gate for auto-instrumentation. When true, the chart renders
the `Instrumentation` CR. Pods still need the matching
`instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-<lang>: "true"` annotation
to be instrumented.
enabled.title: enabled

issuers.description:
name of the VCR resource
- name:
  -- credential type to request (must match one of the issuer's supported types)
  credentialType:
  -- credential format (jwt_vc_json, ldp_vc, jwt_vc, vc+sd-jwt)
  format: jwt_vc_json
  -- name of the target Secret for storing the credential
  targetSecretName:
  -- key in the target Secret (defaults to "credential")
  targetSecretKey: credential
  -- filename when the secret is projected as a volume (for backward compatibility)
  targetFile:
  -- duration before expiry to trigger renewal (e.g. 5m, 1h)
  renewBefore: 5m
  -- additional issuer-specific claims
  additionalClaims: {}
  -- holder binding configuration (enables proof-of-possession during OID4VCI issuance)
  holderBinding:
    -- enable holder binding for this credential request
    enabled: false
    -- name of the Secret to create for the holder's ECDSA P-256 private key (auto-generated with tls.key entry)
    keySecretName:
    -- reference to an existing Secret (if set, key generation is skipped)
    existingKeySecret: ""
    -- optional DID URL for the proof JWT kid header; when omitted the operator embeds the full JWK
    holderDID: ""
several CredentialIssuers, each with its own `name`, `issuerURL`, `issuerType`, `tokenURL`,
`auth` and `requests` as above. When set, it replaces `issuer`, `auth` and `requests`.
issuers.title: issuers

requests.title: requests
